title: The Quadratic Formula — The Ultimate Problem Solver 🚀
hook: What if there was ONE formula that could solve ANY quadratic equation? No factoring, no guessing — just plug in a, b, c and get the answer! That's exactly what the Quadratic Formula does, and it was discovered by the Indian mathematician Shreedharacharya!
explanation:
By completing the square on the general equation ax² + bx + c = 0, we get:
SHREEDHARACHARYA'S QUADRATIC FORMULA
x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a
Part of FormulaWhat It Gives You
−b / 2aThe x-coordinate of the vertex (midpoint of the two roots)
√(b² − 4ac)How far apart the two roots are from the midpoint
The ± signOne root with +, another with − (two solutions!)
💡 Tip: This formula works for ALL quadratic equations — even when factorization is impossible. It's derived by completing the square on ax² + bx + c = 0.
⚠️ Tip: Don't forget: the formula only gives real roots when b² − 4ac ≥ 0. If b² − 4ac < 0, there are no real solutions!
worked_example:
Solve 2x² − 3x − 5 = 0 using the Quadratic Formula:
1
Identify a, b, c
a = 2, b = −3, c = −5
2
Calculate discriminant
b² − 4ac = (−3)² − 4(2)(−5) = 9 + 40 = 49
3
Apply the formula
x = (−(−3) ± √49) / (2 × 2) = (3 ± 7) / 4
4
Find both roots
x = (3 + 7)/4 = 10/4 = 5/2
x = (3 − 7)/4 = −4/4 = −1
ANSWER
Roots: x = 5/2  and  x = −1

fun_fact: While we call it the 'Quadratic Formula' in English, in India it's rightfully called Shreedharacharya's Rule, honoring the 8th-century Indian mathematician who first described this method. Indian mathematicians were solving quadratics centuries before Europe! 🇮🇳
